executive_summary: This collection window (May 4-10, 2027) is the forty-sixth archived window. Per this window's brief, WebSearch specifically checked for Met Gala 2027 post-event coverage now that the Editorial Calendar's first-Monday-in-May date (May 3, 2027) has passed inside the prior window. No reachable red-carpet, theme-execution, or standout-look coverage of the event surfaced -- the same coverage gap flagged in the 2027-05-03 report persists past the event date itself, which is a materially different and more notable gap than a pre-event silence. Dior's Cruise 2027 show (Los Angeles, May 13) and Gucci's Cruise 2027 show (New York) both fall outside this window on either side, so neither is logged as a signal here. No other corroborated, dateable signal met this project's sourcing bar this window; collection_status is set to 'thin' rather than forcing a marginal item into top_signals to fill a quota.
limitations: Met Gala 2027 was specifically re-checked this window for post-event coverage (red carpet, theme execution, standout looks) now that the May 3, 2027 date has passed. No reachable coverage of any kind -- pre- or post-event -- was found: no theme, no co-chair lineup, no exhibition tie-in, no red-carpet photos or best-dressed roundups. This is a stronger and more unusual gap than the 2027-05-03 report's pre-event silence, since major outlets normally publish red-carpet coverage same-day. Logged honestly as an unresolved coverage gap rather than assumed evidence the event didn't happen or was restructured -- unverified secondary chatter about possible 2027 format changes (guest-list downsizing, scaled-back red carpet) exists but is not corroborated by any primary or editorial-sector source and is not logged as a signal.

Dior's Cruise 2027 show (Los Angeles, May 13) and Gucci's Cruise 2027 show (New York) were checked; Dior falls just after this window's close and Gucci's New York Cruise 2027 show was confirmed to have already taken place in 2026 (cruise collections are commonly shown roughly a year ahead of the label year) -- neither is logged as a signal in this window.

Wales Bonner/Hermes and the CFDA Fashion Fund/Awards questions were not re-litigated this window per SKILL.md workflow note 10; both remain 'untracked going forward pending new information' with no new coverage found.
This report was assembled via targeted web search rather than a live automated crawl or direct social-platform API/dataset access, consistent with prior reports' compliant manual-sampling approach.
